primary_citation.popular_name: Freedom of Speech and Press / Shield Law (constitutional)

key_holding: Every person may freely speak, write and publish on all subjects. No law may restrain or abridge liberty of speech or press. Publishers, editors, reporters cannot be held in contempt for refusing to disclose sources or unpublished information.

amendment_history.event: Article I adopted as part of second California Constitution
Prop. 5 (Res.Ch. 77, 1978) — added subdivision (b) shield law provision protecting journalists from contempt for refusing to disclose sources
